description: Structured disposal and recycling knowledge base grounded in India Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and Plastic Waste Management Rules (MoEFCC / CPCB).

categories.description: Corrugated shipping boxes, paperboard cartons, packaging containers, and cereal boxes.

guidance.summary: Cardboard should be segregated as dry waste for recycling, provided it is clean and free of food grease.
do_s: Flatten boxes to optimize space in dry waste collection containers.
Keep cardboard dry and separate from kitchen wet waste.
Hand over clean cardboard to dry waste collection centers (DWCCs) or local scrap aggregators.
dont_s: Do not mix cardboard contaminated with food grease or oil into dry recycling streams.
Avoid leaving cardboard exposed to rain or moisture before collection.
preparation_steps: Empty all contents from the box.
Remove plastic packing tapes and styrofoam inserts.
Flatten the cardboard box.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Proper segregation of cardboard supports paper pulp recovery and prevents dry recyclables from decomposing in landfills.

categories.description: Vegetable peels, fruit scraps, leftover food, coffee grounds, and eggshells.

guidance.summary: Food organics must be segregated as wet waste at source for home composting or municipal organic waste processing.
do_s: Segregate all food scraps and kitchen waste in wet waste bins.
Use home composting or municipal bio-degradable waste collection streams.
Ensure food waste is handed over regularly to local waste collection services.
dont_s: Do not mix plastic wrappers, carry bags, fruit stickers, or metal foil with food waste.
Do not dispose of kitchen food waste in open drains or public spaces.
preparation_steps: Scrape leftover food into the designated wet waste bin.
Remove any synthetic packaging, plastic stickers, or rubber bands.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Composting or biomethanation of wet waste produces organic fertilizer and biogas while preventing methane emissions in dumpsites.

categories.description: Glass beverage bottles, food jars, and glass containers.

guidance.summary: Glass bottles and jars are recyclable dry waste when segregated carefully to prevent breakage.
do_s: Rinse glass containers with water to remove food residues.
Segregate intact glass bottles as dry waste or return reusable glass bottles to deposit schemes.
Handle glass carefully to ensure safety for waste collectors.
dont_s: Do not mix mirror glass, window panes, or ceramic pottery with container glass bottles.
Do not throw broken glass loosely into general collection bins without protective wrapping.
preparation_steps: Rinse container thoroughly.
Separate plastic or metal caps for individual dry waste sorting.
Store safely until dry waste collection.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Glass recycling conserves raw minerals and energy required for cullet melting.

categories.description: Aluminum beverage cans, tin food cans, metal bottle caps, and clean foil.

guidance.summary: Metals have high scrap recovery value and should be segregated as dry waste for recycling.
do_s: Rinse metal cans to remove liquid or food residue.
Segregate clean metal items into dry waste.
Hand over scrap metals to authorized recyclers or local scrap aggregators.
dont_s: Do not dispose of pressurized aerosol cans or chemical containers in general trash unless completely empty and safe.
Do not mix oily or chemical metal containers with clean dry waste.
preparation_steps: Rinse out contents.
Allow metal cans to dry.
Separate non-metal attachments if possible.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Metal recycling significantly reduces energy consumption and industrial mining footprint.

categories.description: Broad heterogeneous category containing composite items, non-standard materials, or mixed non-recyclables.

guidance.summary: This category represents a broad, mixed group of objects. Disposal rules depend on the specific material composition and local municipal authority guidelines.
do_s: Check if any component of the item (metal, hard plastic, paper) can be separated into dry waste.
Consult local Urban Local Body (ULB) rules for reject waste or domestic hazardous waste disposal.
Keep e-waste, batteries, or medical items strictly out of mixed trash.
dont_s: Do not assume all miscellaneous items automatically belong in general landfill waste.
Do not mix hazardous chemicals or electronic accessories into general waste streams.
preparation_steps: Inspect the item for recyclable sub-components.
Separate recyclable parts from non-recyclable non-hazardous rejects.
Follow local municipality guidelines for reject waste management.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Proper sorting of mixed products reduces reject volume sent to sanitary landfills or waste-to-energy plants.

categories.description: Newspapers, office paper, magazines, notebooks, mail, and paper bags.

guidance.summary: Clean, dry paper is a primary recyclable material under source segregation rules.
do_s: Keep paper clean and dry in the dry waste container.
Hand over paper to local dry waste collection centers or scrap aggregators.
Bundle newspapers and cardboard separately for easy handling.
dont_s: Do not mix paper soiled with food, grease, or liquids into dry recycling.
Do not burn paper waste in open areas (prohibited under clean air regulations).
preparation_steps: Remove plastic wrappings, pins, or covers.
Keep paper flat, clean, and dry.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Recycling clean paper saves forest resources, reduces water consumption, and supports local circular supply chains.

categories.description: Rigid plastic bottles, milk jugs, food containers, tubs, and plastic packaging.
categories.general_disposal_category: Dry Waste / Plastic Waste Management Rules

guidance.summary: Plastics should be segregated at source into dry waste for processing under Plastic Waste Management Rules and EPR frameworks.
do_s: Rinse out food or beverage residues from plastic containers.
Segregate clean plastic items into dry waste for collection by local Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) or registered recyclers.
Check for numerical plastic identification codes (#1 PETE, #2 HDPE, etc.) where available.
dont_s: Do not burn plastic waste under any circumstances (causes toxic emissions).
Do not dispose of plastic items in storm drains or water bodies.
preparation_steps: Empty and rinse the container.
Allow to dry before placing in the dry waste bin.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Source segregation of plastics enables mechanical recycling, prevents microplastic accumulation, and supports Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR).

verification_metadata.source_name: MoEFCC & CPCB - Plastic Waste Management Rules & EPR

categories.description: Used clothing, rags, fabric scraps, worn shoes, and household linens.

guidance.summary: Textiles should be kept dry and separate. Usable clothing should be donated; unwearable textiles should go to textile recycling drives or ULB dry waste collection.
do_s: Donate wearable clothing to local shelters or donation drives.
Keep unwearable fabric scraps clean and dry for specialized textile recycling or dry waste collection.
Reuse old cotton fabrics as household cleaning rags.
dont_s: Do not mix wet or soiled textiles into general organic waste bins.
preparation_steps: Wash and dry items.
Separate usable garments from damaged scrap fabrics.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Reusing and recycling textiles extends fabric lifecycles and diverts bulky waste from municipal landfills.

categories.description: Garden waste, leaves, grass clippings, weeds, small plant trimmings, and flowers.

guidance.summary: Vegetation and horticulture waste should be composted or processed through municipal green waste streams.
do_s: Segregate garden trimmings and leaves for home or community composting.
Hand over horticulture waste to municipal green waste collection drives.
Use dry leaves as mulch around plants or trees.
dont_s: Do not burn dry leaves or garden waste (strictly prohibited under clean air regulations).
Do not mix plastic pots, synthetic ties, rocks, or pesticides with vegetation waste.
preparation_steps: Remove plastic tags, pots, or wire ties.
Bundle small trimmings if required by local collection guidelines.
guidance.environmental_impact_note: Composting garden waste enriches topsoil and prevents smoke pollution from leaf burning.
